hero.description: I turn complex problems into elegant code. Whether it's shipping a game mechanic that feels right, or architecting a backend that scales — I build solutions that actually matter to clients.

about.label: About me
about.p1: I'm a freelance software engineer who lives at the intersection of engineering discipline and creative drive. My specialty is game programming — physics systems, real-time rendering pipelines, gameplay feel — but I thrive across the full spectrum of computer science.
about.p2: Every project starts the same way: understanding what you actually need, not just what you asked for. Then I build a solution that fits precisely, performs reliably, and ships on time.
about.p3: When I'm not freelancing, I'm usually deep in a personal game project, contributing to open-source tools, or learning more about new technologies I currently have no experience with.

voidengine.desc: A custom 2D/3D game engine built from scratch in C++17 with an OpenGL renderer, entity-component system, scene editor, and integrated Lua scripting for gameplay logic.

neoncity.desc: A cyberpunk endless runner with procedurally generated city blocks, dynamic obstacle patterns, and a real-time lighting system using Unity's HDRP pipeline.

clientsync.desc: A client relationship manager built for a small consulting firm. Features pipeline tracking, contract management, invoice generation, and Slack integration.

rustnet.desc: A lightweight game networking library in Rust implementing reliable UDP, client prediction, lag compensation, and server reconciliation for multiplayer games.

shaderlab.desc: An in-browser GLSL shader playground with live editing, uniform sliders, texture upload support, and one-click export to Unity-compatible shader code.

logicforge.desc: 48-hour game jam entry — a puzzle platformer where you reprogram the level's logic mid-run. Placed 3rd in the Ludum Dare 54 Compo category.
